They use creative design to prompt human-nature interaction by fostering rich sensory engagement and a sense of play, which invites people to pause and explore the natural world [SOURCE 1]. Specifically, the structures amplify sounds in four locations (e.g., tree crowns, water, woodland) to create immersive, interactive experiences that highlight natural auditory vistas [SOURCE 2]. This design approach emphasizes listening as a way to notice and appreciate nature’s details, offering a "new perspective on the wonders of the natural world" [SOURCE 1]. The playful, sound-based interventions align with broader principles of creating spaces that "invite people to engage with nature" by blending exploration with joy and calm [SOURCE 3].
